Hermes Agent comes to Teams

18 November 2026 · Reading time: 4 minutes

Nous Research is bringing its open-source Hermes Agent to Microsoft Teams, the Microsoft Store and Azure, so employees can hand it work in chat and get the finished result back in the same conversation.

Sapaude retells the story in its own words. The source is below. Publisher: Sapaude.

In three points

Three points, in this order: what the source shows, where that claim stops, and what to check next.

  1. On November 18, Nous Research announced Hermes Enterprise: Hermes Desktop for Windows in the Microsoft Store, Hermes in Microsoft Teams for tasks like financial analysis, document drafts or inbox triage, and agent runs in isolated Azure Container Apps Sandboxes.
  2. Hermes turns a successful approach to recurring work into a reusable skill, a written definition plus code for the stable steps. With Collective Wisdom, employees can propose and publish those skills for their team, with review.
  3. Nous says Hermes Agent is the number one public open agent on OpenRouter, at nearly 2 trillion tokens a day. Prices, customers and independent tests are not part of the announcement.

Hermes moves into Microsoft's tools

Nous Research, the team behind the open-source Hermes Agent, announced Hermes Enterprise in New York on November 18, 2026. The company is part of the portfolio of M12, Microsoft's venture fund. The agent now runs inside the Microsoft services that many companies already use.

There are three entry points. Hermes Desktop for Windows is available in the Microsoft Store. In Microsoft Teams, employees can assign Hermes knowledge work, from financial analysis and document drafts to triaging an inbox, and review the finished result in the same conversation. The agent workloads run on Azure Container Apps Sandboxes, in isolated microVMs that according to Nous start in under a second and release compute when idle.

Nous says Hermes Agent currently ranks number one among public open agents on OpenRouter and processes nearly 2 trillion tokens a day. Both figures come from the company.

Skills from everyday work

The core of the pitch is what happens with recurring tasks. When an employee delegates the same kind of work again and again, Hermes automatically turns a successful approach into a reusable skill. Nous describes it as a written definition paired with code that runs the stable steps the same way every time. Established workflows should then use less inference and become more reliable over time.

A feature called Collective Wisdom takes this to the team. Employees can ask Hermes which of their skills are worth sharing, then propose and publish them for colleagues, with a review step. The next person who takes on the task starts from the best approach anyone on the team has found. Nous says that knowledge remains a private asset of the organization and is not used as training data for an AI vendor.

Own Azure tenant for strict requirements

For organizations with strict data residency, security or procurement rules, Hermes Enterprise can run in the customer's own Azure tenant, under a similar product and pricing model. Nous does not name prices in the announcement.

"Hermes became the most popular open agent because it gets better the more you use it," said Nous Research CEO Dillon Rolnick. Michelle Gonzalez, head of M12, called it "a simple way to put self-improving agents to work". Nous is presenting the product at Microsoft Ignite in San Francisco, including session BRK448 on secure agent loops in isolated sandboxes.

What is still open

The announcement names no customers and no independent measurements. That skills make agents cheaper and more reliable is Nous's own claim. Hermes Enterprise is also a product that a company rolls out: if your employer has not deployed it, Teams does not gain the agent on its own. Results from an agent, especially financial analyses or sorted mail, still need a human check before anyone relies on them.

What you can do

Agents are moving into the chat tools companies already use. Whether Hermes shows up in your Teams is your employer's decision, and the reliability claims are so far the company's own.

In the app, the same story is also told shorter and in more detail, matched to your level.
